channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: 1994 Rwanda genocide suspect arrested in Flemish village
item.description: The man is suspected to have been a key figure in April 1994 massacres at a care home for people with disabilities.

item.title: Airplanes grounded in the USA for safety reasons
item.description: The US FAA orders all flights across the United States to remain on the ground until further notice, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns.

item.title: Too late, too narrow: EU audit of Russia trade sanctions exposes accountability gap
item.description: “EU trade sanctions will deliver their intended impact if all member states apply them in a uniform and coordinated way."

item.title: Microsoft reports ‘improvement’ following global issues affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot
item.description: Several Microsoft cloud services, including Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and Copilot, were disrupted.

item.title: US-Iran war has caused over $200 billion in damage in the Gulf, report shows
item.description: The overall cost of the US-Iran war to Gulf economies is likely to reach $790 billion by 2030, according to an Allianz Trade report.

item.title: Russia arrests two persons accused of working for Polish intelligence
item.description: Two persons have been arrested in Russia on suspicion of spying for Poland’s Defence Ministry and Internal Security Agency.

item.title: US judge refuses to dismiss Trump's defamation suit against the BBC
item.description: Trump is seeking $10 billion from the BBC, including $5 billion for defamation.

item.title: USA: Trio charged with attempted attack on British Air Force base
item.description: US prosecutors lay charges against three men who, they say, planned to attack RAF Fairford, the UK airbase used by the US in its war against Iran.

item.title: Iran deems French cyberattack accusations baseless
item.description: Tehran rejects the 'baseless and one-sided accusations' by the French government against Iran concerning alleged cyber activities in France.

item.title: Belgian dies in light aircraft crash in New Zealand
item.description: A Belgian and a New Zealander were killed when a light aircraft crashed near Castor Peak in New Zealand on 3 November.

item.title: Palestinian doctor seeks court order to force evacuation of family from Gaza Strip to Belgium
item.description: “The constant fear that his loved ones will be killed before he has been able to see them again and hold them in his arms adds to the physical suffering caused by his cancer and reduces his chances of recovery.”

item.title: Kremlin: Peace talks in Abu Dhabi are taking place without Europeans
item.description: The Kremlin has said this week’s talks in Abu Dhabi on ending the war in Ukraine will be strictly trilateral, involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States.

item.title: At least 20 dead in four shipwrecks involving migrant boats off the coast of Crete
item.description: At least 20 people have died, and two are missing after a series of migrant boat incidents off the coast of the Greek island of Crete.

item.title: Europe to be represented at Ukraine War peace talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: The talks are set to take place on Tuesday and Wednesday, involving both Russia and Ukraine. The United States will act as a mediator.

item.title: Flemish Minister-President attends annual World War victim remembrance
item.description: Diependaele emphasised the need to support Ukraine to stop the "Russian steamroller" and protect and preserve Europe's freedom.

item.title: Vincent Kompany expected to return to coaching within a month
item.description: The former Belgian international footballer was rushed to hospital two weeks ago upon collapsing while watching a training session.

item.title: Foreign Minister Prévot expresses condolences after Kraków shooting
item.description: Anyone concerned about relatives or in need of assistance can contact the Belgian embassy in Warsaw.

item.title: Family members of Palestinians in Belgium affected by severe Gaza storms
item.description: The damage to personal belongings has exceeded €3 million as floods swept through Gaza on Friday night.

item.title: US ambassador to Belgium outraged by Brussels synagogue attack
item.description: Bill White visited the synagogue in Anderlecht on Saturday with Israel’s ambassador to Belgium, David Saranga, after the building was targeted in what White called a clear act of antisemitic vandalism.

item.title: Congo wants its human remains back. What will it take for Belgium to return them?
item.description: More than 500 human remains from the DRC, Rwanda and Burundi are still held in Belgium. Some in the AfricaMuseum, but most at the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences.
